maya: Nightly eval flagged a big spike in the 'contradictory_answers' cohort for q4b-llama-v2-small (int4). Failing promptset = instruction_consistency_cohort. Severity: P2 — visible regression in a few customer-facing queries. Can @dena or @igor pick this up? :eyes:
eval-bot: [AUTO][2467890123] suite=nightly_consistency cohort=instruction_consistency quant=q4b-llama-v2-small delta=+18.3% failures -> alert created. Logs: https://internal.redwood/evals/2467890123
samir: I can grab initial logs. Is this only seen on smallbatch (batch_size<=4) runs?
leo: I remember a tiny-kv-cache corner case showing nondet outputs before, but that was different. Do we have raw generations to compare?
dena: I'll own the repro. Have a quick local repro that flips answers between few-shot contexts. Pushing a minimal command below.
```bash
# repro (local)
python eval_runner.py \n  --model redwood/q4b-llama-v2-small \n  --suite instruction_consistency \n  --seed 42 \n  --batch-size 2 \n  --kvcache small \n  --quant int4 \n  --log-output repro/2467890123.json
```
dena: Example failing snippet from repro: "Q: Is Earth the center of the solar system?
A (shot1): Yes
A (shot2): No" — same prompt, different shots.
igor: pinging eng-runtime to check if batching or KV cache path might introduce state reuse across requests. @eng-runtime-team
samir: I'll pull token-level logits and compare int4 vs fp16 for the same seed, will post diffs in this thread.
leo: quick experiment suggestion: try running with `--kvcache off` and `--batch-size 1` to isolate caching/batching effects.
dena: initial hypothesis: quant attention kernel + cached KV under small context causes precision drift that flips top tokens in a few sensitive prompts. Running runs for: (int4+kvcache), (int4+kvcache off), (fp16+kvcache). Will report numbers.
eval-bot: owners assigned: dena, igor. severity=P2. followup_deadline=EOD. tickets: ENGML-7832, ENGRUN-441.
maya: Thanks — if anyone can paste one failing prompt and the raw outputs (two shots) that reproduce, we'll decide whether to push a narrow rollback for the dedicated pools or add a canary guard. :thumbsup:
